title: Norman Granz and the hardships of road travel
summary: Hall credits Norman Granz with raising wages and ending discrimination in hotels and travel.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Right. So what happens between, you know, and we weren't making that much money when we were playing there either. People like Hawk and Edmond Hall and Perez, they died from desperation, like what's the use, you know? They were contributing all along. Couldn't get anywhere. Only Roy stuck it out, and that's because of Norman Granz. (nonsense) Norman Granz saved the situation. He changed that around, as far as engagements go, hiring guys.
-- the wages and the general attitude.

Nondiscriminating in the hotels, plane travel and -- these guys, when I -- the reason I didn't want to go on the road, riding around in a touring car that never made a successful trip. Something would break down, and you're going to be late for the job.
Uh-huh, you're going to be eating greasy hamburgers.
